newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat condition improves with mild weather.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat condition improves with mild weather.

text.p: Texas's wheat crop improved amid a return to more mild, open weather conditions during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop report.
The dry weather allowed producers to make good progress on land preparations in the Plains, and planting operations moved ahead in South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley.
Increased growth and greening were noticed in many wheat-growing regions during the week, and the report said insect populations were also increasing but were not serious yet.
Wheat was rated 11 percent excellent, 49 good, 34 fair and six poor. That compared to last week's rating of nine percent excellent, 45 good, 38 fair, seven poor and one very poor.

Range and pasture conditions were rated five percent excellent, 28 good, 43 fair, 17 poor and seven very poor. That compared to last week's ratings of five percent excellent, 29 good, 41 fair, 18 poor and seven very poor.
Texas cotton acreage was one percent planted, compared to three percent last year and three percent for the five-year average. Corn was 11 percent planted, versus 24 last year and 17 for the average.
